item.title: Kill Goofy — Sun Oct 25, 1:30 PM — Grove Street Theater
item.description:
Apricot Sky Productions’s new play, Kill Goofy by Livingston playwright Eric Alter, opens October 9 and plays for three weekends throught October 25. The story is simple on the surface. Two best friends, inseparable at thirteen, haven’t spoken in thirty years. One of them never left his childhood bedroom. His mother never left because someone had to take care of him. Then the other one comes back to town, and everyone in that house has been keeping the same secret. It’s a play about the things we never say to the people closest to us, and it sends people out the door talking. Please note the play deals with difficult subject matter and is recommended for ages 15 and up. The full synopsis and content advisory plus more information are at https://apricotskyproductions.com/killgoofy. Share this: Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook

item.title: American Ethos Concert — Sun Oct 25, 3:00 PM — Glen Ridge Congregational Church
item.description:
As part of the Glen Ridge Community Concerts series, join us Sunday, Oct 25, at 3 pm, for a multi-media recital, “American Ethos” performed by pianist Carolyn Enger. The program reminds us of the unique spirit of America and the different cultures that make up our nation. Her repertoire shines a light on diverse, often overlooked voices, as well as more well-known composers of our time. Selections include works by Leonard Bernstein, Aaron Copland, Craig Urquhart, Daron Hagen, John Corigliano, Margaret Bonds, Florence Price, Ned Rorem, Meredith Monk, Margaret Ruthven Lang, Robert Sirota and William Grant Still. item.title: Stronger Montclair Election Conversation — Mon Oct 26, 6:00 PM — Montclair Main - Auditorium
item.description:
Stronger Montclair is hosting a conversation at Montclair Public Library. Join us as neighbors and friends to discuss some of the issues facing the Township Council within the context of the Strong Towns Movement as we approach Election Day.
We plan to share a respectful conversation between residents of Montclair, in which participation is encouraged, to discuss issues such as the spiraling cost and the shortage of housing, shuttles and local transportation, parking and curbside management, safe streets for all users, and a sustainable, transparent local government finance.
This is not a structured debate or forum, rather an opportunity for individuals to be heard. The Township Council candidates are invited to participate as residents, with the same time constraints as everybody else. As we conclude, we’ll allow each candidate in attendance to make a statement limited to three minutes.
Registration is not required but recommended for event updates.
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306

item.description:

Join us for an open feedback session to share whatever is on your mind:
How you use the library today
What you love about our programs, collections, and spaces
Frustrations or obstacles you've run into
What you’d love to see in the renovated space
Whether you have big design ideas or just want to tell us about your favorite books, we're all ears. Your feedback will directly guide the design, programs, and future of our library.

How do I sign-up?
Register here or in the Student Rec Center main office, or over the phone (973-655-3340). Cost for Students $20

item.title: “Troilus and Cressida” (Workshop) — Sat Nov 21, 7:30 PM — Life Hall Studio Theatre 1200
item.description:
Directed by: Katherine Wilkinson | Written by William Shakespeare Troilus and Cressida (play) is a dark, satirical take on love and war during the Trojan War. Troilus and Cressida’s romance is tested when she is traded to the Greek camp, while warriors and leaders on both sides reveal ambition, ego, and moral decay. The play questions heroism, loyalty, and what’s left of love in a world defined by conflict.
Montclair State University Students FREE with ID at Kasser Box Office
Hosted by: The College of the Arts

item.title: Clean-Life Living — Sat Oct 24, 3:30 PM — Union Congregational Church
item.description: From Hip-Hop to Holistic Health: Clean-Life LIVING Brings Fresh Perspectives on Living Well to Montclair Darryl “DMC” McDaniels, Dr. Brian Clement, Warren Zanes and other notable guests come together October 24 for an afternoon of inspiration, connection and community benefiting Montclair Helps. MONTCLAIR, NJ — What do a hip-hop legend, a holistic wellness pioneer, a rock musician and bestselling author, a community builder and a scholar of American transcendentalism have in common? More than you might think. On Saturday, October 24, Montclair will host Clean-Life LIVING, an afternoon designed to explore what it means to live well in an increasingly complicated, demanding and often disconnected world. Taking place from 3:30 to 6:30 p.m. at Union Congregational Church, the event brings together an eclectic group of speakers whose experiences span music, nutrition, psychology, creativity, philosophy and community building. item.title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776” — Sat Oct 24, 7:00 PM
item.description: The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013. Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ. The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. item.title: Inner Body Meditation (20 Minutes) — Sat Oct 31, 10:45 AM
item.description:
The Mindful Stream "Awareness of the inner body takes you beyond the mind." - Eckhart Tolle
In this mediation session we will bring our attention here: to the inner body. Sessions are suitable for newcomers, those experienced in Tolle's teachings and anyone wishing to remain completely anonymous. They will last around 20 minutes and cameras and microphones will be disabled.
(Depending on the situation, a free discussion may be held at the end with mics and cameras allowed.)
See you there!
Please be aware that sessions will close if no members have joined after 10 minutes.
Emrys also organises a free Work of Byron Katie online mediation group. Visit [this Meetup Group link](https://www.meetup.com/thework-runsfree/) for more information.
